findings.reason: naming the plan-review gate as prior art forces the plan to justify a fourth bespoke override field (`orchestrator_lane_override`) against the existing three, and to state the reason-string addition as the thing that makes this fence more than a copy.
findings.text: the plan rebuilds, for the orchestrator lane, the exact refusal-plus-explicit-override-plus-recorded-field shape the plan-review gate already ships (`D23` discharge in `refusals.py`; `--allow-unreviewed-plan`; `unreviewed_plan_override` recorded at `dispatch.py:6783` and `ledger.py`), and never cites it — only the sibling's *count* of such sites. The design should say whether it extends that shape (a shared recorded-override idiom) or is a deliberately separate fence, and should carry the reason-string difference as the stated distinction.

findings.reason: the plan must name `refusals.py` as the discharge owner and budget the census-test change, or the refusal half of §1 ships with an unregistered discharge and no census row.
findings.text: §1's stated end state is a refusal that "names the lane … and names a discharge", but the implementation composes the discharge in two new inline helpers (`_orchestrator_lane_discharge_candidates`, `_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop` at `dispatch.py:4381-4475`) instead of registering a family in `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES` and rendering through `format_refusal`, the one owner every other dispatch refusal uses and the census test `tests/test_crew_refusal_visibility.py:82` pins as an exact set. As landed the stop is advisory, so nothing is broken yet; the moment §4 flips the severity to `refused`, the plan produces a refusal site whose discharge lives outside the registry — exactly the "refusal sites against discharges" gap the plan cites in its own sibling. Extend `refusals.py`: add a `D24` family (updating the census's expected set) and render the discharge through `format_refusal`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the fence's whole judgement is one function, `_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop`, returning a self-describing verdict; §3's multi-surface spread is text parity, not a second implementation of the fact.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the stop composes and renders its own discharge beside `reckon/crew/refusals.py`, the single owner of dispatch-refusal discharge text that the refusal-visibility census enumerates.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites its sibling's discharge census and the flight-config key, but names none of the machinery it actually repeats: the plan-review gate's refusal-plus-override shape and `reckon/crew/refusals.py` as the discharge owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the declaration rides the existing declared-backend-property idiom (`metered`, `budget_group`, `fallback` all say "declared, never inferred"), the override rides the existing ledger override field, and §4 states why the stop is advisory rather than a refusal and when it flips.
